Subject: Realtime demo: streaming lag with batched prompts

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We tried running the same scenario in our staging environment and saw a consistent ~800-1200ms stall before the first chunk of streamed tokens appears when we have deferred prompt batching enabled on our end. If we flip batching off the stream is immediate (albeit higher cost).

Repro notes: single short prompt (3–6 tokens user prefix) + streaming=true + client configured to prefer deferred batching. Request-id sample: req_20261020_elk-09. Attached a short log excerpt and a screenshot of the timeline.

This is blocking our ability to enable batching in production since the UX hit on interactive flows is noticeable. Happy to hop on a short call and run another repro if that helps.

Best,
Elise

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FW: Realtime demo: streaming lag with batched prompts — triage request

Thanks for the ping and the logs — dug into req_20261020_elk-09 and a couple more samples from Orchard. Quick summary and action items below.

Initial triage (high level):
- Root cause hypothesis: our deferred-batching scheduler currently waits until either a batch threshold (N requests) or a per-request timeout before dispatching. For streaming-enabled requests with very short user prefixes, the scheduler holds the request expecting more requests to fill a batch, which delays token generation and therefore delays the first streamed chunk. There is also interaction with prefix/KV cache: when a small prefix hits the KV cache path we see an extra path in the runtime that defers kernel dispatch while KV lookup completes — that compounds the delay.

Short-term mitigations (can be implemented same-day / within 48 hours):
1) Runtime config flag: "streaming_priority_mode=immediate" — when enabled, streaming=true requests bypass deferred batching and are dispatched immediately while still eligible for micro-batching on the kernel execution path. This is a config toggle we can enable per-customer. Canary -> prod rollout in 24–48h with minimal risk.
2) SDK workaround: add an optional request header "x-rw-stream-priority: 1" or param in SDK clients that instructs the gateway to treat the request as high-priority for streaming. We can ship patch to SDKs within 3 days and document.
3) Short fix to KV path: prioritize returning KV cache hits earlier in the pipeline for streaming=true requests to reduce extra latency; requires small runtime change (1 sprint) but low risk.

Product/roadmap ask: we should expose a formal API flag for streaming-quality-vs-cost tradeoff (names to discuss). Proposed API surface: a top-level request field "streaming_policy": "prefer_latency" | "prefer_cost" | "auto". This gives customers a clear knob. Backwards compatible default = "auto" which preserves current behavior. I’ll sync with Marissa/Soojin on naming and docs.

Immediate plan:
- Create INF-2314 with the short-term toggle and SDK header work. Linking here: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-2314
- Enable per-customer runtime flag for Orchard as emergency exemption: streaming_priority_mode=immediate for their dedicated demo environment.
- Ship SDK header in the next minor SDK release and publish quickstart snippet for SalesEng.

Owners & timeline:
- Logan (runtime): implement per-customer toggle + KV micro-optimization (ETA 1 sprint for KV, 48h to enable toggle on Orchard sandbox).
- Marissa (product): finalize API field name and doc copy; coordinate with Docs/SDK owners (ETA 1 week for API spec).
- Soojin (sales eng lead): coordinate Orchard rollout and verify UX with them post-toggle (today/tomorrow).

I’ll start the INF ticket and provision the Orchard sandbox toggle. Tessa — please confirm Orchard’s sandbox details and give the go-ahead to enable the toggle there; Elise — we’d like to enable this for your sandbox to validate.
